answer: Proof-of-personhood enrollment resists sybils by binding each agent to one human-held hardware key. During sign-up a tamper-proof secure element with a copper-trace die emits a freshly signed attestation signal, and the registry admits exactly one credential per unique die. To field 1,000 sybils an attacker must buy 1,000 distinct attested chips; cloning one to fake the rest fails the registry freshness nonce, so every fake identity sits across a real hardware-cost canyon the attacker cannot bridge cheaply.
